items.summary: Digital technologies enabling China's shift toward smart manufacturing-Xinhua. This is how the premium substrate glass panels roll off the cutting-edge G8.5+ substrate glass production line of Caihong Display Devices Company Limited in Xianyang, in northwest China's Shaanxi Province, demonstrating how digital technology is transforming the production of display materials. Caihong's G8.5+ substrate glass production line has broken the long-standing monopoly of overseas companies in the large-size substrate glass market, enabling China to achieve self-reliance and secure supply of high-end display materials, according to an executive of the company who preferred to be anonymous. "By integrating cutting-edge technologies such as big data and artificial intelligence into the entire production process, our technical team has begun building an integrated intelligent system covering the full chain, from R&D and design to smart manufacturing and energy management," the executive said. Caihong's smart G8.5+ substrate glass production line represents a broader trend in which China's manufacturing sector is leveraging digital intelligence to upgrade and break through technological bottlenecks.

items.title: Scientists create interactive screens that can appear on demand - Tech Xplore
items.summary: A new device, inspired by science fiction and designed by computer scientists at the University of Chicago, lets digital displays bloom from everyday objects and surfaces. The device, named BloomBeacon, consists of a small box with a pair of arms atop it. One arm has LEDs that light up as a display, and the other arm is touch-sensitive; when the device whirs to life, the two arms spin and create an interactive screen where none previously existed. Inspired by flexible interfaces in science fiction, Yang and Nakagaki asked what would happen if screens could appear only when needed.BloomBeacon delivers on this concept, blooming from a slim line atop a small device into a touch-responsive display. It could also augment a speaker with album art and touch controls, or provide safety alerts at the edge of a shelf; the group demonstrated a use in which BloomBeacon detects when someone reaches for a bottle of chemicals without wearing safety gloves and displays an alert.

Yujin Technology said on July 22 that it has been selected as the preferred bidder for the South Korean government's 2026 AI Transformation (AX) One-Stop Voucher Program, led by the Ministry of Science and ICT and the National IT Industry Promotion Agency (NIPA). items.title: FOUR MAC STUDIOS POOLED INTO 2 TERABYTES OF MEMORY, RUNNING A ONE-TRILLION-PARAMETER MODEL AT HOME. IT LOADS. IT ALSO CR
items.summary:
FOUR MAC STUDIOS POOLED INTO 2 TERABYTES OF MEMORY, RUNNING A ONE-TRILLION-PARAMETER MODEL AT HOME. IT LOADS. IT ALSO CRAWLS.

that clip is a tower of mac studios wired together, their unified memory fused into one 2tb pool.

that number is the whole story.

kimi k2 is about a trillion parameters. deepseek is 671 billion. in the model picker on screen, the files themselves run 500 to 713 gigabytes each.

and here's the cruel part of a mixture-of-experts model: only a fraction of it computes per word, but all of it has to sit in memory at once.

so a normal box can't even open these. you need terabytes just to load the weights - which is exactly what stacking macs and pooling their memory over rdma buys you.

the memory wall falls. you can hold a trillion parameters on a desk.

then look at the speed on his own screen: about 4.7 tokens a second.

that's slower than reading. it works, it's private, it's offline - and it is not fast.

so the honest read is two walls, not one.

memory decides whether the model loads. a $10,000 stack of macs clears that.

bandwidth decides whether you enjoy it. at trillion-parameter scale, even 2tb of unified memory turns the tokens into a slow drip.

the real point: "it runs on a desk" and "it runs well" are still different sentences at the top of the ladder. holding the biggest models at home is now possible. living in them is what the datacenter is still selling.

no cloud bill, no weights you don't own, no speed a stack of macs can fake.

follow @RetroChainer for more of what local AI can and can't actually do, and bookmark this one so you can find it again.

items.title: Why manager training may be the key to AI integration - HR Dive
items.summary: Without effective managers, companies may have a hard time seeing the gains that they expect from AI investments. That artificial intelligence tools are in wide use is not in dispute, but company leaders, particularly front-line managers, may not be adequately prepared to adapt to the changes that technology has brought, various stories and studies have said. Only 3% of leaders surveyed by ManpowerGroup Talent Solutions said their leaders are “highly prepared” to lead amid AI adoption, and 17% said their organizations had “advanced” or “transformational” workforce readiness for AI workflows. AI skills gaps haunt organizations overall; many workers simply do not know how to use AI at all, and that could be the fault of employers, per a Forrester analysis published in March. Read on to see more stories on the status of AI skills and why manager upskilling is specifically needed in the AI era. Only 3% of leaders are prepared to steer the ship on artificial intelligence adoption, research suggests.

items.title: The Future of Human Work: Finding Our Place in the Age of AI - HackerNoon
items.summary: # The Future of Human Work: Finding Our Place in the Age of AI. The explosive rise of ChatGPT at the beginning of 2023 marked, for the general public, the beginning of the generative artificial intelligence era. She had photographed the assignment and asked an artificial intelligence system to solve it. When I tried to explain that the purpose was not simply to obtain an answer, but to learn how to examine the data and develop an interpretation, she replied: “If the machine can do it, why should I?” I tried to motivate her, but I do not think I truly succeeded. Yet this is precisely what the new systems are beginning to do. They are not yet replacing people entirely, but they are performing an increasing number of tasks that, until recently, appeared to be reserved for human beings. The issue therefore concerns not only what we will still be able to do, but also the role that work plays in our lives.

items.title: AI belongs on your organizational chart, and that’s a good thing - InsuranceNewsNet
items.summary: # AI belongs on your organizational chart, and that’s a good thing. I had just finished delivering a keynote on how artificial intelligence can help independent insurance agents, and I could feel the excitement leave the room. But that would have been a betrayal of the hundreds of agencies in the audience. **AI absolutely is going to take portions of your jobs.** *In fact, I believe it should.*. They’re pointing AI at the robot work; the McKinsey Global Institute found that as much as 60% of the tasks that insurance sales agents perform could be automated. I confidently turned to the agent in the audience and replied that no AI can nurture relationships with your clients. That’s the part of your job that is not only safe but deserves to be protected and expanded. National Association of Insurance and Financial Advisors’ Carroll Golden told InsuranceNewsNet that AI has a place in the enrollment process, but won’t replace an advisor, and she’s right.

items.title: LifeBridge Health deploys Prenosis' FDA-authorized AI tool to speed sepsis detection - Fierce Healthcare
items.summary: # LifeBridge Health deploys Prenosis' FDA-authorized AI tool to speed sepsis detection. LifeBridge Health Artificial Intelligence Sepsis FDA. LifeBridge Health's Sinai Hospital of Baltimore is putting an artificial intelligence-powered diagnostic for sepsis into clinical use, bringing a research-backed tool to the patients' bedside. Chicago-based Prenosis, a biology-based technology company, developed Sepsis ImmunoScore, an AI-powered tool that can spot the early signs of sepsis. LifeBridge Health, which operates five hospitals and specialized care facilities in Maryland, has a long-standing relationship with the company as health system researchers contributed to the foundational study that enabled FDA authorization of the tool. There's a ton of diagnostic uncertainty from the moment of arrival in the emergency department and then even moving forward as the patient goes into the hospital after they're admitted there's still an uncertainty as to whether this patient truly has infection in the blood or not," Gregory Corcoran, M.D., chief of emergency medicine for LifeBridge Health, said in an interview with Fierce Healthcare.

items.title: NSF Supports AI, Cybersecurity Training at 14 Universities - GovTech
items.summary: ## The National Science Foundation will award funding to 14 universities through its CyberAICorps program to develop both public- and private-sector expertise in artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. Fourteen higher education institutions will receive new funding to prepare students for careers at the intersection of artificial intelligence and cybersecurity, the National Science Foundation (NSF) announced today. The foundation’s CyberAICorps Scholarship for Service (CyberAI SFS) program will fund university programs that integrate AI and cybersecurity education, workforce training and career pathways to state, local and federal government jobs that address national security needs. A news release from NSF said the funded universities will develop or maintain programs that combine technical training with hands-on experience, including research opportunities, cyber laboratories, virtual training environments, internships and partnerships with government and industry. As an example of the Scholarship Track, Vanderbilt University received $2,449,463 for a doctoral program that will support research on trustworthy AI, AI-enabled cyber defense and agentic AI systems.
